title: Least-Favourable Rank Coupling for Multi-Arm Contrast Covariance in the Causal Bootstrap
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the sound package incremental below the field floor and found no bounded in-scope repair: the polynomial-recognition-or-sharp-hardness and binary-witness-completeness upgrades require genuinely new mathematics.
gap_reasons: The note proves an exact graph-Laplacian criterion for a prespecified scalarized oracle covariance loss and a two-opposite-columns classification for universal Loewner dominance under uniform fixed-count assignment.

The practically broader nonexchangeable-kernel problem receives only factorial/exponential enumeration through generic copositivity tests, with recognition complexity and the witness alphabet left open.

The package also assumes oracle knowledge of every armwise potential-outcome marginal and supplies neither feasible marginal estimation nor an inference or coverage theorem, limiting its econometric usefulness relative to the causal-bootstrap framing.

Resolve the computational core of general-balanced-kernel: give a polynomial-time exact recognition algorithm for rational admissible balanced kernels, or a sharp hardness result paired with a nontrivial tractable subclass, and determine whether binary witnesses are complete.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved exact graph-Laplacian and Loewner classifications for uniform fixed-count multi-arm designs, including optional unassigned units, a sharp 2/N regret identity, binary necessity witnesses, and exact recovery of the finite Aronow–Green–Lee oracle design. It also reduced the nonexchangeable balanced-kernel branch to finite copositivity and exact algebraic certification. The field claim collapsed because this general branch still needs polynomial recognition or admissibility-preserving hardness, a tractable subclass, and binary-witness completeness or a least-alphabet theorem; feasible marginal estimation and coverage remain a separate statistical extension.
tldr: Under every uniform fixed-count sample-and-assign design with positive arm counts and an optional unassigned remainder, the common-rank potential-outcome completion is universally least favourable for the scalarized covariance loss \(\operatorname{tr}\{W\operatorname{Cov}_Z(C\widehat{\bar Y})\}\) if and only if \(H=C^{\mathsf T}WC\) is a graph Laplacian.  The count-independent \(O(K^2)\) certificate has an exact \(2/N\) regret identity and a one-success counterexample for every feasible design outside the cone.  Full covariance dominance occurs only for two nonzero opposite columns of \(C\).  The two-arm result exactly recovers the finite Aronow--Green--Lee sample-then-treat law, Equation (2), and its comonotone oracle endpoint.  On the separate \(K\mid N\) balanced-kernel domain, finite cut copositivity is exact and decidable for algebraic inputs, while polynomial recognition and the minimal complete witness alphabet remain open.
gap: Sharp rank completion is analytic for the two-arm difference-in-means estimator, whereas generalized causal-bootstrap work uses integer programming for broad designs and estimators. The literature does not state the exact contrast-geometry boundary at which one common-rank completion remains universally least favourable in a multi-arm experiment, nor a label-invariant recognition problem restricted to realizable nonexchangeable balanced covariance kernels.
fill: The project derives the complete-randomization risk decomposition, proves the graph-Laplacian iff theorem by pairwise rearrangement and isolated binary necessity witnesses, evaluates both mechanisms exactly at \(K=3,N=6\), classifies the Loewner case, and uses cut generators to characterize the identity-optimal cone over covariance tensors induced by valid balanced assignment laws modulo unit relabelling.
